Erik Underwood

Approval Voting candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Colorado · Open seat

Candidate for Colorado governor (occupation not confirmed in the sources reviewed)

Erik Underwood is the Approval Voting Party nominee for Colorado governor in the Nov. 3, 2026 general election, with Frank Atwood as his running mate for lieutenant governor. He calls himself an independent Democrat and says he ran at the Democratic state assembly in spring 2026, finished second, and did not reach the threshold for the primary ballot. He then got a ballot spot through the Approval Voting Party.

Where Underwood stands

Housing and cost of living
Proposes state-backed home loans at 2.75% through a new housing division, state-owned homes, converting empty office buildings into affordable housing, housing zones to keep rents down, and rent freezes where needed.
TABOR and state budget
Plans to prepare a ballot measure to eliminate TABOR. Says Medicaid grows about 9% a year while TABOR lets the budget grow about 3%.
State budget / structural deficit
Proposes saving money by ending private prison contracts, cutting outside consultants, and using the state's buying power to lower prescription drug costs, instead of cutting services.
Taxes
Supports higher taxes on extremely wealthy residents.
Homelessness
Opposes criminalizing people for sleeping in parks. Proposes more shelters, mobile crisis teams, mental-health care, addiction treatment, and transitional housing.
Water
Says Colorado's protections are the Colorado River Compact and prior appropriation. Says he will not accept a river deal where Colorado agriculture is the only water that gets cut.
Technology regulation (data centers)
Proposes a moratorium on data centers starting his first day in office because of their water and power use. Says he would not approve AI data centers that use millions of gallons of water for cooling.
Energy and environment
Would not expand oil and gas development beyond current levels. Opposes fracking near reservoirs, drinking water, and wildlife areas. Says communities should decide which developments they accept.
Health care and education
His priorities include universal health care, child care support, and free college and trade school.
Voting age
Supports lowering the voting age to 16 and plans to propose a bill to do so in his first year.

Background

  • 2026: Approval Voting Party nominee for Colorado governor, with running mate Frank Atwood
  • 2026: Sought the Democratic nomination at the state assembly; finished second and did not reach the threshold for the primary ballot
  • Raised by a single mother in housing projects; oldest of six children
